validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + STATUS confirmed independently of gem.wiki's own citations (2 of 4 harvested citations were dead/inaccessible - see note at end). Energy Transfer LP's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-02-16, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1276187/000127618724000024/et-20231231.htm) states in present tense: 'We also own a 70% interest in Red Bluff Express Pipeline, which owns a pipeline in the Delaware Basin' and lists it as an active asset in its intrastate pipeline table (70% / 120 miles / 1.4 Bcf/d). These are two separate SEC registrants (majority owner/operator Energy Transfer and minority owner Western Midstream), each with independent audit/reporting obligations - genuinely independent corroboration. Anadarko Petroleum's FY2018 10-K also corroborates the asset's existence from a third company's perspective (as a shipper/area operator). No existence or classification concern.

Western Midstream's FY2022 10-K asset table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1423902/000142390223000023/wes-20221231.htm) explicitly tags the line 'Gas' (vs. 'Oil'/'NGLs' for its other equity investments in the same table). validity.recommendation: Update LengthKnown from 80.00 mi to ~120 mi (current per FY2022/FY2023 10-Ks of BOTH owners); GEM's 80 mi does not match the pipeline's length in any Energy Transfer or Western Midstream annual filing from 2018 onward.
validity.researcher_notes: MATERIAL, well-corroborated length discrepancy. GEM's sheet has LengthKnown=80.00 mi. Energy Transfer's own 10-Ks report the pipeline's mileage growing over time: FY2018 10-K (filed 2019-02-22) states 'a 100-mile intrastate pipeline system' and its asset table lists '100' miles; FY2019 10-K (filed 2020-02-21) states 'an approximately 108-mile intrastate pipeline' (108 in the table) after 'An expansion of the Red Bluff Express Pipeline' entered service in 2H2019; FY2022 10-K (filed 2023-02-17, ~7 months before this row's LastUpdated of 2023-09-05) and FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-02-16) both state 'an approximately 120-mile intrastate pipeline' (120 in the table). Critically, Western Midstream's FY2022 10-K - a SEPARATE SEC registrant, the 30% minority owner, filed independently of Energy Transfer - lists the same investee at exactly '120' miles in its own equity-investment table. Two independently-reporting companies agree on 120 miles as of FY2022, the period closest to this row's LastUpdated. GEM's 80 mi is below even the earliest (2018, pre-first-expansion) reported figure of 100 mi, so it is not explainable as a stale-but-once-correct value from initial construction; it appears to be simply wrong, or possibly a partial-segment figure (gem.wiki's talk page breaks it into 65mi@42in + 10.4mi@36in + 6.2mi@30in = ~81.6mi, suspiciously close to 80, suggesting GEM may have summed only a subset of construction-phase diameter segments rather than using the pipeline's total mapped length). Not applying the fix directly - flagged as a concern per the sweep's read-and-stage-only rule; recommend Update leg apply LengthKnown=120.00 with the refs below.
